description: Device pairing v3 (PROTOCOL 10.2, ADR 0033 3): v2's commitment, reply and opening, hybrid with ML-KEM-768. pair_key = HKDF-SHA256(secret, salt="", info="z-pair-key-v3", 32). The new device offers a fresh ML-KEM-768 key ek beside its commitment, c = HMAC-SHA256(pair_key, "z-pair-commit-v3:" || eph_n || ded || dx || SHA-256(ek) || sk || id), where sk = SHA-256 of the new device's own sealing key; the existing device answers with its ephemeral and (ct, K) = ML-KEM-768.Encaps(ek; m); the opening adds sk to v2's fields. channel_key = HKDF-SHA256(dh || K, salt=pair_key, info="z-pair-channel-v3", 32); the SAS is eight digits of HKDF-SHA256(dh || K, salt=eph_n || eph_e, info="z-pair-sas-v3" || ded || dx || sk || id || SHA-256(ek || ct), 8), from seven bytes as in v2. The mailboxes and the rendezvous are derived as v2's under "z-pair-relay-v3:" and "z-pair-rendezvous-v3:". The enrolment is v2's without "root", which v3 never carries, and with "pqdc", the root's attestation of the new device (ADR 0033 1), here 3 309 recorded random bytes that pairing carries unread. version_2_of_the_same_inputs is what v2 computes from the same ephemerals and device fields; a v3 client computes none of it. K, ct and the KEM keys are re-derived from kem.seed and kem.m by kyber-py.
